card.title: Triangle, parallelogram and polygon laws of vectors

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Scalars — mass, time, energy — carry magnitude only and add arithmetically; vectors — displacement, force, velocity — carry direction and add geometrically. The **triangle law** places vectors head to tail; the **parallelogram law** draws them from a common point and takes the diagonal: $R = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2 + 2AB\cos\theta}$ at angle α with $\tan\alpha = B\sin\theta/(A + B\cos\theta)$ — giving A + B when parallel,…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - R = √(A² + B² + 2AB cos θ) - tan α = B sin θ / (A + B cos θ) - R_max = A + B (θ = 0°); R_min = |A − B| (θ = 180°); θ = 90° → R = √(A² + B²)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Speed vs velocity:** speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity); velocity is a vector — a body in circular motion has constant speed but changing velocity. %%+ **Distance vs displacement:** distance is the scalar path length; displacement is the vector from start to finish and can be zero over a closed path.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Vectors add nose to tail — never arithmetically."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***10 N and 20 N at 60°*** — resultant √700 ≈ 26.5 N at 40.9° from the 10 N force (NEB 2021).

rows.text: Verified PYQs: parallelogram numerical (2021, 5m); component addition (2021, 3m); scalar vs vector (2020, 2m).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Adding Quantities That Refuse to Add Masses add: 3 kg + 4 kg = 7 kg. Displacements do not: 3 m east then 4 m north is not 7 m of anything. Quantities that need a direction — displacement, force, velocity — are **vectors**, and they obey geometric laws of addition. This topic covers scalars vs vectors, and the triangle, parallelogram and polygon laws.  ·  ## 2. rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "R² = A² + B² + 2AB cos θ — cosine, not sine, in the magnitude."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): Two forces of 5 N and 12 N act at right angles. Find the resultant.** — R = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 N; tan α = 12/5 → α = 67.4° from the 5 N force. Perpendicular vectors make the 2AB cos θ term vanish.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Most-tested: the 5m parallelogram numerical (2021) and component addition (2021). Always give magnitude AND direction.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Vector addition is commutative but direction-dependent:** A + B = B + A, yet the resultant's magnitude depends critically on the angle between them.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Scalars add arithmetically; vectors add geometrically (triangle/parallelogram/polygon laws).  ·  Parallelogram law: R = √(A² + B² + 2AB cos θ); tan α = B sin θ/(A + B cos θ).  ·  Special cases: θ = 0° → A + B; 90° → √(A² + B²); 180° → |A − B|.  ·  Polygon law: head-to-tail for many vectors; a closed polygon means zero resultant (equilibrium).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The maximum resultant of two forces is A + B and the minimum is |A − B| — any question asking for bounds uses these two limits.

rows.text: ## 3. The Laws of Vector Addition ### 3.1 Triangle law If two vectors are drawn **head to tail**, the resultant is drawn from the tail of the first to the head of the second (closing side of the triangle). $\vec R = \vec A + \vec B$ — the order does not matter (commutative: $\vec A + \vec B = \vec B + \vec A$).…  ·  ## 4. Worked Numericals (NEB 2021) **Q (5m, 2021):** Two forces P = 10 N and Q = 20 N act at a point with 60° between them. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant. *Given:* P = 10 N, Q = 20 N, θ = 60°. *Formula:* $R = \sqrt{P^2 + Q^2 + 2PQ\cos\theta}$; $\tan\alpha = \dfrac{Q\sin\theta}{P + Q\cos\theta}$.…  ·  ## 5. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 4 (resolution):** the parallelogram law and resolution are the same idea run in opposite directions — combining vs splitting. - **To Topic 5 (products):** the dot and cross products give compact formulas for the angle between vectors.…
